lines.trans: Everyone around the courtyard has their teacups raised—go ahead and place it in, Nour.
Wrapped tight in yellow waxed linen, resting dry and level on the clean river sand.
Notice we kept the brass compass upstairs on the front desk where maps belong.
And in its place, seven friends leave a warm hello for thirty summers ahead!
Ready to slide the flat stone back over the brick pocket with Tariq, Mazen?
Watch your fingers, boss—lower the north edge first, then let it settle flat.
Not a wobble anywhere! Tap it once with your wooden handle for good luck, Tariq.
Solid, level, and ready for table number one for the next thirty Mays.
Look up through the tree branches at those rooftop lanterns shining against the evening sky!
When Monday morning started two weeks ago, I worried about one swapped blue suitcase.
Now look at Jasmine Courtyard House: nine full rooms, twenty-eight neighbours, and music every week!
Before you get misty-eyed again, boss, help me hang that framed map inside.

meanings.note: Reinforces negation ('not at all, never'): ما في زبدة أبدا ('no butter at all'), لا تقلق أبدا ('do not worry at all').

examples.trans: There is no butter in the fridge at all!
Do not worry at all, sir.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: زرقا, plural: زرق).

examples.trans: The blue suitcase is in the luggage closet.
I have two blue teacups.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صفرا, plural: صفر).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.
The yellow lemon cake is ready.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Jordan, Syria, Lebanon and Palestine use the old Syriac-derived month names: كانون التاني January ... أيار May ... أيلول September.

examples.trans: My birthday is in May.
In May the weather gets nice in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a finger or toe; dual إصبعين ('two fingers'), broken plural أصابع.

examples.trans: Pull the paper out gently with two fingers.

examples.text: خلي أصابعك بعيدة عن الفرن السخن.
examples.trans: Keep your fingers away from the hot oven.

meanings.note: Introduces 'that'-clauses with pronoun suffixes (إنه 'that', إني 'that I', إنك 'that you', إنها 'that she/it') and appears in إن شاء الله ('if God wills').

examples.trans: Thank you for coming today.
Do you think that I am a hotel inspector?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The reception desk is beside the door.
Thank you for the warm welcome.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of الاثنين ('Monday', and with ال also 'both / the two').

examples.trans: I started work on Monday morning.
Monday's bus arrived at seven.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنتبه, بينتبه).

examples.text: انتبه على راسك من الخشب الواطي.
examples.trans: Watch your head on the low beam.
Be careful of the corner chair.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببدا, بيبدا).

examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.
The day began lively and bright.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'then, next, afterwards' (وبعدين 'and then').

examples.trans: Lift the handle first, and then push.
Have some tea and then we will talk.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for a navigation compass (بوصلة النحاس 'the brass compass'). Plural: بوصلات.

examples.trans: The brass compass always stays at the front desk.

examples.text: رسمنا بوصلة صغيرة على بطاقة الترحيب.
examples.trans: We drew a small compass on the welcome card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بيوت.

examples.trans: The old house has a lovely courtyard.
The neighbourhood houses are built of stone.

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتحرك, بيتحرك).

examples.text: في قطعة معدن تحركت جوا الصندوق!
examples.trans: A piece of metal shifted inside the box!
The car pulled away from the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: تحيات.

examples.trans: Here is to all our kind neighbours!
He returned the greeting with a warm smile.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بترك, بيترك).

examples.text: مين ترك هاد المغلف جنب الجرس؟
examples.trans: Who left this envelope by the bell?
Thank you for not leaving me in the rain.

meanings.note: Numeral 'nine'; short form تسع (tisa') before a plural noun (تسع دقايق 'nine minutes').

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

تفضّل.gloss: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!
Here you go, hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'thirty'.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian all-purpose word for 'all set, fine, spot-on!'.

examples.trans: Everything has to be spot-on!
Alright, I can remember the sentences.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بثبت, بيثبت).

examples.trans: Hold still a moment and listen to that sound!

examples.text: الكرسي ثبت بعد ما شدينا البرغي.
examples.trans: The chair held firm once we tightened the screw.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: جيران.

examples.trans: All the neighbours on the street are kind.
Good morning, dear neighbour.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Active participle of إجا ('to come'): means 'on the way / arriving' (جايين 'they are coming') and after a time noun 'next' (الأسبوع الجاي 'next week').

examples.trans: The guests are coming down the stairs now.
We will see you next week!

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('inside the bag') and standalone ('inside').

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Masculine noun for a pocket or hollow recess (جيب الطوب 'the brick pocket'). Plural: جيوب.

examples.text: هداك الجيب تحت الحجرة مبطن بطوب.
examples.trans: That pocket under the stone is lined with brick.
He put the small key in the coat pocket.

meanings.note: Feminine noun for the rim of a tin or the edge of a paving stone (الحافة الشمالية 'the north edge'). Plural: حواف.

examples.trans: We wrapped white tape around the rim of the tin.
Lower the north edge first gently.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حجار.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحط, بيحط).

examples.trans: Where should I put the spoons and napkins?
I put the suitcase beside the table.

meanings.note: Everyday masculine noun (حظ حلو 'good luck'). Plural: حظوظ.

examples.text: دق الحجرة دقة وحدة عشان الحظ الحلو!
examples.trans: Tap the stone once for good luck!

examples.text: من حسن الحظ لقينا المفتاح بدرج المكتب.
examples.trans: By good luck we found the key in the desk drawer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: حلوة, plural: حلوين).

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: خرايط.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أخشاب.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافية, plural: دافيين).

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بدق, بيدق).

examples.trans: My heart is beating fast!
The clock tower started chiming twelve.

meanings.note: Covers daqqa ('a knock / clock chime', pl. دقات) and diqqa ('precision / punctuality', الدقة بالمواعيد).

examples.text: سمعنا اطنعشر دقة من برج الساعة.
examples.trans: We heard twelve chimes from the clock tower.
I always love punctuality.

meanings.note: Form II verb (بتدمّع / دمّعت) from دمع ('tears'). Used when someone's eyes well up with emotion.

examples.text: قبل ما تدمّع عيونك يا معلم، ساعدني!
examples.trans: Before your eyes get misty, boss, help me!
Her eyes watered with joy at the gift.

meanings.note: Form II causative of رجع ('come back').

examples.trans: I put the keys back in the desk drawer.

examples.text: هاد اللحن القديم بيرجعنا لأيام زمان.
examples.trans: This old melody takes us back to the old days.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برفع, بيرفع).

examples.trans: Lift the handle first and then push.
He raised his cup in a toast to the neighbours.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرقام.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for sand (رمل النهر 'river sand'). Plural: رمال.

examples.text: حطينا العلبة على رمل النهر النضيف.
examples.trans: We rested the tin on the clean river sand.

examples.text: الرمل تحت البلاط لازم يكون مستوي.
examples.trans: The sand under the tiles must be level.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بساعد, بيساعد).

examples.trans: He will surely love to help us!
We helped the guest carry her suitcase.

meanings.note: Numeral 'seven' (عالسبعة 'at seven o'clock').

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I booked room seven yesterday.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطوح.

examples.trans: We heard the sound of rain on the roof.
From the rooftop we see the hills of Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سماوات.

examples.trans: The evening sky is clear and calm.
The lanterns are glowing beneath the sky.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Singulative noun ('one tree') of collective شجر ('trees').

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from شمال ('north'). Feminine: شمالية (الحافة الشمالية 'the north edge').

examples.text: نزّل الحافة الشمالية أول يا معلم.
examples.trans: Lower the north edge first, boss.
The northern rooms are a bit cooler in summer.

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for wax (شمع عسل 'beeswax') or candles (singulative شمعة).

examples.text: لفينا العلبة بقماش شمع العسل الأصفر.
examples.trans: We wrapped the tin in yellow beeswax cloth.
We put small candles beside the lanterns.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word (from Turkish çanta) for any handbag, backpack, or travel suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.
We set the suitcases beside the reception desk.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صحاب.

examples.trans: Who is the owner of the blue suitcase?
We became friends from the first day.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

ضوّى.gloss: to light up; shine; switch on a light

meanings.en: to light up; shine; switch on a light
meanings.note: Used for a lamp that glows and for the person who switches it on (ضوي الضو 'turn on the light').

examples.trans: The new lamp gives good light.
Turn the light on, the room is dark.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: طاولات.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Collective noun for bricks or building blocks; حيط طوب is a brick wall.

examples.trans: The house is built of brick and stone.
They brought new bricks for the wall.

عشان.gloss: for; because of; in order to

meanings.en: for; because of; in order to
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'for / because of' (عشان هيك 'that is why') and 'so that'.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: Numeral 'twenty' (followed by a singular noun in Arabic: عشرين دقيقة 'twenty minutes').

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعلق, بيعلق).

examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror?
We hung the lanterns in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; also used in the delighted Jordanian exclamation يا عيني! ('oh my! / how lovely!').

examples.trans: Close your eyes and smell the coffee!
Oh my, look at that warm light in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: غرف.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فوانيس.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns are lit in the courtyard.
We hung a brass lantern by the entrance.

meanings.note: Masculine noun used both literally for tree branches and figuratively for shop branches. Plural: فروع.

examples.trans: Let's leave it by the almond branch.

examples.text: هاد الفرع قريب من وسط البلد.
examples.trans: This branch is close to downtown.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فناجين.

examples.trans: I set two teacups on the tray.
This is my favourite coffee cup.

meanings.note: Used both before a noun ('above, over') and standalone ('upstairs').

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Means 'before' (قبل الفطور) and with a time span 'ago' (قبل ساعة 'an hour ago', قبل شوي 'just now').

examples.text: علمت بيانو هون قبل خمسة وعشرين سنة.
examples.trans: I taught piano here twenty-five years ago.
Drink your coffee before the rush.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'in front of, before'.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns against the evening sky.
The car is parked in front of the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
examples.trans: I taught piano in a house near here.
We booked a table at a nearby restaurant.

meanings.note: Levantine adjective on the فَعْلان pattern from root ق-ل-ق; often followed by على ('about').

examples.trans: Why do you look so worried?
We were worried about you the whole way.

meanings.note: Any fabric; سلك قماش is old cloth-covered electrical wire.

examples.trans: She bought blue fabric for the curtains.
This fabric is very soft.

meanings.note: Arabic uses no 'is/are' in the simple present, while كان supplies the past ('was/were') and يكون / بيكون supplies future or modal 'be'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Question word 'how?'.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Form III verb (بلاحظ / لاحظت) from root ل-ح-ظ, common in both formal and everyday Jordanian speech.

examples.trans: Do you know what I noticed first?
I didn't notice that the window was open.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Negates verbs and في (ما بعرف 'I don't know', ما في 'there isn't'), and links conjunctions like قبل ما ('before') and بعد ما ('after').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Passive participle of the quadriliteral verb بروز ('to frame', from برواز 'frame').

examples.trans: It'll be framed before dinner.
The framed photo is hung in the living room.

meanings.note: Form V participle from root ب-د-ل ('exchange'), describing things that have been switched around.

examples.trans: The three keys are swapped here.
The weather is changeable this week.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.
The air is calm and pleasant this evening.

meanings.note: Form VIII participle from root س-و-ي. Means level/flat for surfaces, and 'well-cooked/ripe' for food.

examples.trans: Put it on a level surface.
The table isn't level, it wobbles.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Passive participle of فرد ('to spread/unfold'), describing flat sheets of paper or rolled dough.

examples.trans: They stayed flat inside the box.
The papers are spread out on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أماكن.

examples.trans: This place is very quiet and comfortable.
Everything is tidy in its proper place.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ملفوفة, plural: ملفوفين).

examples.text: شو هاد الشي الملفوف بورق أبيض؟
examples.trans: What is this thing wrapped in white paper?
The parcel is wrapped with great care.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مليانة, plural: مليانين).

examples.trans: All the hotels on our street are full tonight!
The pot is full of hot mint tea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'good' and adverbially 'well' (نمت منيح؟ 'did you sleep well?').

examples.trans: It has a good, comfortable wooden bed.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: We found an old music book in the suitcase.
Gentle music is soothing in the evening.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناشفة, plural: ناشفين).

examples.trans: Here is a dry towel for your coat.
The attic is dry and warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نايمة, plural: نايمين).

examples.trans: The new guest is sleeping on the third floor.
The whole neighbourhood is asleep and quiet.

meanings.note: In Jordanian Arabic, نحاس covers both yellow brass and red copper, often placed directly after a noun (مفاتيح نحاس brass keys).

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: نظيفة, plural: نظاف).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the room is ready.

examples.text: آسف نقطت مي على أرضكم النظيفة.
examples.trans: Sorry I dripped water onto your clean floor.

meanings.note: Masculine noun for a river (like نهر الأردن 'the Jordan River'). Plural: أنهار.

examples.text: من قعدة عند النهر سنة خمسة وتسعين.
examples.trans: From sitting by the river in ninety-five.
The water is very clear in this river.

meanings.note: Jordanian spoken feminine distal demonstrative ('that one over there'), matching masc. هداك.

examples.trans: Open the drawer under that screen.
That table is close to the window.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Used both as the numeral 'one' and after a noun for emphasis ('a single, one and the same').

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ياسمين.

examples.trans: The jasmine vine climbs above the door.
The evening scent of jasmine lifts the spirit.

meanings.note: For door handles and bag handles, Jordanian speakers often say يد الباب / عاليد alongside إيد for the human hand.

examples.text: ارفعي يد الباب أول وبعدين ادفعي.
examples.trans: Lift the door handle first, then push.

examples.text: في بطاقة مربوطة على يد الشنتة.
examples.trans: There is a tag tied to the handle of the bag.
